report.summary: Self-verification within the same model family provides limited independent signal on code tasks. Measurements show marginal gains (e.g., Self-Refine improved pass@1 on MBPP by ~5.6% without execution feedback; Self-Debugging without execution saw ~3.8% improvement). With execution feedback, gains are substantial (Reflexion: +17.7% on HumanEval). Cross-family verification is under-measured but expected to reduce correlated errors. Error correlation within a family is high due to shared training data and biases. Consensus: pure self-verification is unreliable; external feedback (tests) or diver
risks: Self-verification leads to overconfidence and repeated mistakes due to correlated errors.
Cross-family verification may introduce calibration issues if verifier is weaker.
Execution feedback requires secure sandboxing (fail-closed constraint).
Published numbers may not transfer to Daedalus' specific codebase and model mix.
todos: Prioritize test-based verification wherever possible (e.g., run candidate code in sandbox).
If model-only verification is needed, use a verifier from a different model family to reduce error correlation.
When only one family is available, use majority voting across multiple samples with varied temperature.
Implement a fallback protocol: if verifier and claimant are same family and no tests pass, flag for human review.
Log verification outcomes to measure actual error correlation in your setting.

name: q27-verifier-same-family
question: When the verifier is the same model family as the claimant, how much independent signal remains? What has been measured about self-verification, cross-family verification, and the correlation of errors within a model family on code tasks?
